nodes.title: Calculus with Algebra and Trigonometry
nodes.prereq_text: Qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam.

requires.text: Qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam

nodes.description: Math 3A with precalculus: A function approach integrating algebra, trigonometry, and differential calculus. Topics include: one-on-one and onto functions; inverse functions; properties and graphs of polynomial, rational, exponential, and logarithmic functions; properties and graphs of trigonometric functions; analytic geometry; functions and limits; derivatives; techniques and applications of differentiation; introduction to integration; logarithmic and trigonometric functions.

nodes.title: Calculus with Algebra and Trigonometry
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: Math 3B with precalculus: A continued review of relevant topics from precalculus (see Math 2A); integral calculus, including definite and indefinite integrals; techniques of integration, introduction to sequences and series; with applications in mathematics and physics.

nodes.title: Calculus with Applications, First Course
nodes.prereq_text: Qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam.

requires.text: Qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam

nodes.description: Differential Calculus including analytic geometry, functions and limits, derivatives, techniques and applications of differentiation; introduction to integration; logarithmic and trigonometric functions.

nodes.title: Calculus with Applications, Second Course
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 3A with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: Integral calculus including definite and indefinite integrals, techniques of integration; introduction to sequences and series; with applications in mathematics and physics.

nodes.title: Linear Algebra with Applications
nodes.prereq_text: Math 2B or 3B or 3BI with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: Systems of linear equations, matrix algebra, determinants, vector spaces and subspaces, basis and dimension, linear transformations, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, diagonalization, and orthogonality.

nodes.title: Calculus for Social and Life Sciences
nodes.description: Introduction to differential and integral calculus with applications to modeling in the biological sciences.

nodes.title: Calculus for Social and Life Sciences
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A or 3A or 34A or 34LA with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Continued study of differential and integral calculus with differential andintegral calculus with applications. Introduction to mathematical modeling with differential equations. Calculus of several variables including an introduction to partial derivatives.

nodes.title: Calculus for the Life Sciences
nodes.description: Applications of differential and integral calculus to the life sciences. Includes mathematical foundations, biology examples, and computer programming to simulate dynamic systems.

nodes.title: Calculus for the Life Sciences
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A or 3A or 34A or 34LA with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Applications of differential and integral calculus to the life sciences. Includes mathematical foundations, biology examples, and computer programming to simulate dynamic systems of more than one equation.

nodes.title: Introductory Biology I
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 1A-B-C with a grade of C- or better (Chem 1C may be taken concurrently), or a score of 4 or better on either the Advanced Placement Chemistry or Advanced Placement Biology exams.

items.text: a score of 4 or better on either the Advanced Placement Chemistry or Advanced Placement Biology exams

nodes.description: Introduction to biochemistry, cell biology and development, and genetics.

nodes.title: Introductory Biology II--Physiology
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 1A and Chemistry 1A-B-C with a grade of C- or better; or MCDB 1A with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Introduction to animal and plant physiology.

nodes.title: Introductory Biology Laboratory I
nodes.prereq_text: Grade of C- or better in MCDB 1A (may be taken concurrently).
nodes.description: Laboratory investigations illustrate basic principles of biochemistry, molecular and cell biology, development, genetics & physiology.

nodes.title: Molecular Genetics I: Prokaryotes
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 1A-B, EEMB 2; and, Chemistry 1A-B-C; completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: From the double helix and genetic code to the latest breakthroughs. Structure, function, evolution and manipulation of DNA, RNA. Replication, expression, recombination, complementation, and their regulation in prokaryotes (bacteria, plasmids, viruses). Recombinant DNA technology in medicine, research, agriculture and industry.

nodes.title: Molecular Genetics I: Prokaryotes - Honors
nodes.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in MCDB 101A; consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Honors section designed to permit an in-depth analysis of topics relating to genetics.

nodes.title: Molecular Genetics II: Eukaryotes
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B, and MCDB 101A. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Mendelian and molecular genetics. Replication, recombination, transmission and expression of DNA in eukaryotic organisms from yeast to man. Uses of traditional genetics and modern molecular techniques, including molecular genetic approaches to the study of human disease.

nodes.title: Molecular Genetics II: Eukaryotes - Honors
nodes.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in MCDB 101B; consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Honors section designed to permit an in-depth analysis of topics relating to genetics.

nodes.title: Molecular Genetics Laboratory
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 101A-B or EEMB 129; MCDB 101B may be taken concurrently. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Current molecular genetics techniques used to study model organisms. Module1 - Forward genetics: Mutagenesis and genetic mapping of mutants using single nucleotide polymorphisms, classical Mendelian inheritance. 2) Reverse genetics: gene knockdown by RNAi. 3) Genetic analysis of cell signaling. 4) Cellular reprogramming using transgenic strains. Techniques: PCR, gel electrophoresis, Computer based sequence analysis, fluorescence and light microscopy and imaging. Experiments are based on ongoing research at UCSB. Students get to design their own experiment in final module.

nodes.title: Cell Biology
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, and EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B. Completion of all listed prerequisites wita grade of C or better.
nodes.description: An introduction to the structure and function of cell organelles; membranes, nucleus, mitochondria, chloroplasts, endoplasmic reticulum, golgi apparatus, lysosomes, microbodies, microtubules, cilia, centrioles, and microfilaments.

nodes.title: Cell Biology - Honors
nodes.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in MCDB 103; consent of instructor.
nodes.description: The overall goal of MCDB 103H is to extend the concepts covered in MCDB 103 and apply them to the context of research. For each selected topic, students read a short review article in the first week which provides the historical background and current consensus, followed by a landmark research article in the following week. The course is in the format of journal club with an emphasis on open discussion. Each week, a group of students give an oral presentation and lead class discussion.

nodes.title: Laboratory in Molecular Cell Biology
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, and EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B, and MCDB 103 (may be taken concurrently). Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Laboratory techniques of modern cell biology; molecular dissection of cell structure and function.

nodes.title: Biochemistry - Structure and Function of Macromolecules
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, and EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B; and Chemistry 1A-B-C; and Chemistry 109A-B-C (Chem 109C may be taken concurrently). Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Introduction to the structures and functions of proteins, including enzymes, with emphasis on their basic architecture and biological mechanisms of action and regulation. Methods used for characterizing proteins and analyzing enzyme kinetic data are also emphasized.

nodes.title: Biochemistry - Structure and Function of Macromolecules - Honors
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 108A or MCDB W 108A (may be taken concurrently). Consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Honors component of MCDB 108A or W108A designed to permit an in-depth consideration of selected aspects of the structure/function relationships of proteins and nucleic acids.

nodes.title: Biochemistry - Bioenergetics, Enzymology, and Metabolism
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 108A or MCDB W 108A with a grade of C or better.Chem 109C with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Principles of human energy metabolism. Chemistry and physiology of the major metabolic pathways of energy production. Metabolic interrelationships of the major body organs. Applications to human nutrition and disease, exercise, starvation, obesity, and atherosclerosis.

nodes.title: Biochemistry - Computational & Systems Biology
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 108A-B with a grade of C or better or MCDB W 108A and MCDB 108B with a grade of C or better; Physics 6A-B-C with minimum grade of C (Physics 6C may be taken concurrently); Math 34A-B with a grade of C or better or Math 3A-B with a grade of C or better or Math 2A-B with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Models of Biochemical and Cellular Systems. Introductory systems-biology approach to model the design and the function of biological systems. Students will develop an intuition about physical concepts that are fundamental to discuss how biological organisms acquire and process information from the environment. Those concepts and tools will cover probabilities and basic dynamical systems theory. Students will build models of processes of increasing complexity, ranging from viral dynamics, bacterial resistance to drugs, the maintenance of homeostatic equilibrium (trp operon), biological oscillators (mitotic clock) and genetic switches underlying cellular decisions (bacteriophage lambda and lac operon).

nodes.title: Laboratory in Biochemistry
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 108A or MCDB W 108A; and MCDB 108B; and MCDB 1A-1B. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Laboratory techniques in biochemistry. Focus will be on contemporary biochemical techniques used in biomedical research including the analysis of proteins, recombinant DNA expression and protein purification, enzyme regulation, steady-state kinetic analysis and metabolic control. Emphasis will be on both theoretical and practical aspects.

nodes.title: Principles of Biochemistry
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 1A-B-C; and Chemistry 109A-B. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: An introduction to molecular structures and mechanisms of living systems.

nodes.title: Human Physiology
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, and EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Fundamentals of human physiology at the molecular, cellular and organismal levels. Emphasis on homeostatic mechanisms regulating intercellular communication, muscle function, circulation, metabolism and body fluid balance/composition.

nodes.title: Human Physiology - Honors
nodes.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in MCDB 111; consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Honors section designed to permit an in-depth analysis of topics relating to fundamentals of human physiology at the molecular, cellular and organismal levels. Emphasis on homeostatic mechanisms regulating intercellular communication, muscle function, circulation, metabolism and body fluid balance/composition.

nodes.title: Developmental Biology
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, and EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B, and EEMB 3; and MCDB 101A or EEMB 129. Completion of all listed prerequisties with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Modern aspects of animal development. Molecular and cellular mechanisms of embroygenesis.

nodes.title: Developmental Biology - Honors
nodes.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in MCDB 112; consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Honors section designed to permit an in-depth analysis of topics relating to the mechanisms of animal development, from single cells to the whole organism, using examples from vertebrates and invertebrates studied in terms of morphology, physiology, genetics and biochemistry.

nodes.title: Laboratory in Developmental Biology
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B, and EEMB 3, and MCDB 101A, and concurrent enrollment in MCDB 112. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Modern laboratory techniques in developmental biology. Experimental aproaches to development using several animal model systems.

nodes.title: Plant Development
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, and EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B; and, MCDB 101A or EEMB 129. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Differentiation and morphogenesis of plants: mechanisms of cell-cell interactions.

nodes.title: Experimental Strategies in Physical Biochemistry
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 108A or MCDB W 108A or Chemistry 142A with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Presentation of selected contemporary concepts and methodologies for determining the structure, size, shape, charge, and interactive behavior of biological macromolecules.

nodes.title: Basic Pharmacology
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 101A (may be taken concurrently) or Chemistry 142C; Chemistry 109A-B-C. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Covers a wide range of drugs with a focus on drugs used to treat disorders of the nervous and cardiovascular systems, antibacterial agents, antivirals, and anticancer drugs. Also looks at the pharmacology of inflammation and coagulation. The goal is to understand the underlying physiology behind disorders of these systems and the mechanisms of the drugs used to treat them. Additional out-of-class hours are necessary.

nodes.title: Pharmacology Lab I
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 126 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of C; or MCDB 126A with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: Analysis of drug sites and machanisms of action using isolated tissues, organs, and intact animal preparations.

nodes.title: Basic Pharmacology
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 101A or Chemistry 142C; Chemistry 109A-B-C. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Receptor signaling mechanisms; pharmacology of neurotransmitter and hormone receptors; molecular and cellular mechanisms of drug-receptor interactions.

nodes.title: Basic Pharmacology II: Hormone and Neurotransmitter Receptors and Signaling- Honors
nodes.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in MCDB 126B; consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Honors section designed to permit an indepth analysis of topics relating to receptor signaling mechanisms; pharmacology of neurotransmitter and hormone receptors; molecular and cellular mechanisms of drug-receptor interactions.

nodes.title: Pharmacology Laboratory II
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 126B (may be taken concurrently).
nodes.description: An introduction to molecular and biochemical techniques in pharmacology; drug-receptor binding; receptor isolation; pharmacokinetics; techniques to evaluate potency, concentration and effects of hormones and their receptors.

nodes.title: General Microbiology
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 101A; Chemistry 109A-B-C (Chem 109C may be taken concurrently), or Chemistry 109A-B and MCDB 110. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Focuses on the general biology in microbes, primarily prokaryotes. Topics include the structure, physiology, and development of microorganisms and microbial communities, their culture and control, microbial genomics & metagenomics, and the importance of diverse microbes in food, agriculture, ecology and medicine.

nodes.title: Laboratory in General Microbiology
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 131 (may be taken concurrently).
nodes.description: Laboratory experiments dealing with the isolation, cultivation, and physiological, biochemical and genetic analysis of diverse microorganisms.

nodes.title: Bacterial Pathogenesis
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 101A with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: The mechanisms by which bacterial pathogens cause disease. Investigation of the bacterial gene products that are produced during infection to understand the metabolic, physiological, and genetic factors that contribute to the virulence of bacterial pathogens.

nodes.title: Bacterial Pathogenesis Laboratory
nodes.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in MCDB 132.
nodes.description: The latest molecular, biochemical, and genetic techniques available for theidentification of microbial gene products that contribute to infection. Study of the regulatory parameters that govern their expression.

nodes.title: Molecular and Cellular Immunobiology
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 101A with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Introduction to the current concepts of immunology. Emphasis on immunoglobulin structure and function, cell-cell cooperation in the immune response, and the role of major histocompatibility complex and cytokines in regulating immune responsiveness.

nodes.title: Immunobiology-Honors
nodes.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in MCDB 133.
nodes.description: Honors component of MCDB 133 focusing on selected aspects of the immune system and its components using a web browser to run interactive computer assignments.

nodes.title: Molecular and Cellular Immunobiology Lab
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 133 with a grade of C or better (may be taken concurrently).
nodes.description: Introduction to modern laboratory methods in immunology; properties and characterization of immunoglobulins and immunoglobulin-secreting cells; introduction to hybridoma technology; characterization of effector and regulatory T cells using functional assays.

nodes.title: General Animal Virology
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 101A or EEMB 129 with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: An introduction to the biology of animal viruses with emphasis on the biochemical and biophysical properties of viruses; the mechanisms by which animal viruses replicate; the cellular effects of and response to viral infection; and selected aspects of medical virology.

nodes.title: General Animal Virology-Honors
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 101A; concurrent enrollment in MCDB 134. Completion of all prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Honors virology course designed to permit an in-depth consideration and analysis of selected aspects of the biology and biochemistry of animal viruses, the mechanisms by which they replicate, and mechanisms of antiviral innate immunity.

nodes.title: Cellular Growth Control and Oncogenesis
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 101A-B with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Focuses on mechanisms of growth control of eukaryotes. Topics include: the properties of mammalian cells in culture and how they relate to malignant cells, growth factors and their receptors, cell cycle control, oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes.

nodes.title: Cellular Growth Control and Oncogenesis - Honors
nodes.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in MCDB 135; consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Honors section designed to permit an in-depth analysis of topics relating to Cellular Growth Control and Oncogenesis.

nodes.title: Cytokine Action and Viral Pathogenesis
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 101A and MCDB 101B (101B may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: Honors virology course designed to permit an in-depth consideration of selected aspects of the mechanisms of action of cytokines, with emphasis on the antiviral properties of interferons and their roles in host to viral infection and viral pathogenesis.

nodes.title: Medical Immunology
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 101A OR EEMB 129 with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: By focusing on recent groundbreaking advances in our understanding of the vertebrate immune system, this course explores the contrasting mechanisms of protective immunity against parasites and cancer with various immune disorders that mainly stem from immune dysregulation, such as autoimmunity, acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS), allergies, and other diseases. By engaging in interactive, case-based computer exercises, students will have an opportunity to emulate the discovery of the underlying biological defects that give rise to these and other immune-related diseases.

nodes.title: Medical Microbiology
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, and EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B, and EEMB 3. Completion of all prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Study of the characteristics of bacteria and viruses, both pathogenic and adventitious, as they are associated with diseases of humans.

nodes.title: Medical Microbiology - Honors
nodes.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in MCDB 139; consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Honors section designed to permit an in-depth analysis of topics relating to Medical Microbiology.

nodes.title: Recombinant DNA Methods
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 101A-B and 110; or MCDB 101A-B and MCDB 108A-B-C (MCDB 108C may be taken concurrently); or MCDB 101A-B and MCDB W 108A and MCDB 108B-C (MCDB 108C may be taken concurrently). Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Basic techniques of molecular cloning. Screening of recombinant cDNA libraries, polymerase chain reaction, restriction endonucleases, gel electrophoresis, DNA sequencing, nucleic acid hybridization.

nodes.title: Post-translational Protein Processing
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 108A or MCDB W 108A or CHEM 142A or CHEM W142A with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Structure/function relationships in interesting macromolecules isolated from marine organisms. Focus is on well-characterized pathways from horseshoe crabs, abolones, mussels, and fish as well as others.

nodes.title: Stem Cell Biology in Health and Disease
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 1A-B-C with a minimum grade of C; MCDB 1A-B, EEMB 2-3 with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: Basic biology of embryonic and adult stem cells and nuclear transfer, with emphasis on latest findings from the current literature.

nodes.title: Neurobiology I: Cellular Organization and Biophysics of the Nervous System
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 1A and 1B. Completion of both prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Properties of the nervous system ranging from single cells to the whole organism, using examples from vertebrates and invertebrates studied in terms of morphology, physiology, and behavior.

nodes.title: Neurobiology 1: Cellular Organization and Biophysics of the Nervous System - Honors
nodes.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in MCDB 151; consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Honors section designed to permit an indepth analysis of topics relating to the properties of the nervous system ranging from single cells to the whole organism, using examples from vertebrates and invertebrates studied in terms of morphology, physiology, and behavior.

nodes.title: Neurobiology II: Molecular and Cellular Neurobiology
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 1A-1B and MCDB 151; completion of all prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: This second course of a three quarter neurobiology course sequence (151/152/153) covers both top down systems level approaches and bottom up molecular approaches to major topics in neurobiology. These topics include mechanisms of sensory transduction, processing of sensory information within the brain, mechanisms of muscle control, cell signaling, neuronal plasticity, neuronal polarity, and the mapping of neural information to the brain.

nodes.title: Neurobiology III: Developmental Neurobiology
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 1A-1B; and, MCDB 101A or EEMB 129; completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: The course begins with fertilization and moves through sequential stages in the development of the nervous system, including cell migration and differentiation, axon outgrowth and pathfinding, programmed cell death, synaptogenesis, learning, memory, neurodegenerative conditions and current strategies for neuronal regeneration.

nodes.title: Research Immersion in Molecular Biosciences
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 1A-B with a minimum grade of B in each.
nodes.description: Intensive laboratory course covering basic approaches to biomedical research using model systems. Students will learn laboratory techniques as well as hypothesis building, experimental design, data analysis and data presentation.

nodes.title: Programming in Biology
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B; and MCDB 101A or EEMB 129 (may be taken concurrently); and Pstat 5A or Pstat 5LS or Math 4A. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Studying complex biological systems can be greatly facilitated by modern computing technologies. This course introduces essential computer programming concepts and algorithms to biology major students. Students learn logics of programming and apply it to gene sequence analysis (bioinformatics), simulation of dynamic systems (systems biology), and data analysis (statistics in biology).

nodes.title: Biological Dynamics
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B; and MCDB 101A or EEMB 129; and either Math 4A OR MCDB 108C. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: An introduction to mathematical models and computer simulations used to describe and understand time varying biological systems. Learning Objectives: Survey mathematical methods for describing the dependence on time of biological phenomena. Illustrate how to construct mathematical models to gain insights into complex biological systems. Develop working knowledge of a python code base that enables future evaluation of common classes of models applied to the study of biological dynamics.

nodes.title: Pharmacology Colloquia
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B, and EEMB 3 with a minimum grade of C or better in each prereq course.
nodes.description: Research seminars on current research topics in pharmacology presented by invited speakers.

nodes.title: Literature in Plant Molecular Biology
nodes.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Critical reading and presentation of the current literature in plant molecular biology, cell biology and development.

nodes.title: Special Topics
nodes.prereq_text: Chem 1A-B-C with a minimum grade of C; MCDB 1A-B and EEMB 2 with a minimum grade of C. Upper-division standing in EEMB or MCDB and consent of instructor or department.
nodes.description: Special topics of current importance in biological sciences. Course content will vary. Information may be obtained in department office.

nodes.title: Group Studies for Advanced Students
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Oral reports by students.

nodes.title: Bacterial Genetics.
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Oral reports by students.

nodes.title: C. Elegans Development and Behavior
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Reports by students.

nodes.title: Dissecting the Behavior of Mosquito Disease Vectors
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: This course will focus on the latest developments in understanding how mosquito disease vectors find human host, and mate. The focus will be on mechanistic studies, particularly those that combine molecular genetics with behavior.

nodes.title: Developmental Biology
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Oral reports by students.

nodes.title: Advanced Topics in Neurobiology
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Literature-based exploration of core concepts in modern neuroscience. Skill in training in critical reading of primary literature, science writing, and presentation. Content focus changes each year: past topics include Neuroethology, Neuronal Identity, Motor Control, Sensory Motor Integration, Optogenetics and Functional Imaging.

nodes.title: Immune Cell Biology and Immunotherapy
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Will focus on recent literature related to immune cell biology and cancer-immune interactions. Students will read and discuss a paper each week. The students will alternate as discussion leaders. As discussion leader they will prepare a short presentation to facilitate discussion. Some background in immunology, cell biology and genetics is required.

nodes.title: Neural Circuits
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Presentation and discussion of current research in circuit-level neuroscience. This course will focus on how neural circuits mediate specific behaviors, drawing on research from a range of species and preparations.

nodes.title: Plant Development Genetics
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Oral reports by students.

nodes.title: Biostatistics
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Statistics is an important tool to convey scientific discoveries with a quantitative measure of significance and confidence. In this group study, practical issues in applying statistics to biological data will be discussed.

nodes.title: Systems Medicine
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Explores systems medicine through computational modeling of physiological circuits. Students will develop Python simulations to understand hormone circuits, immune system behavior, and aging processes. Combines theoretical foundations with hands-on modeling exercises to examine how diseases emerge from circuit fragilities. Through mathematical modeling and computational analysis, students will investigate complex physiological systems and learn disease classification based on signaling topology. Students will gain both theoretical knowledge and applied computational skills while exploring how feedback, robustness, and emergent behaviors influence health and disease.

nodes.title: Cell Biology Topics
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Select current topics in the field of cell biology (e.g. cell division, intracellular protein transport, and cytoskeleton dynamics) and discuss how these new findings advance our understanding of cell physiology and behavior.

nodes.title: Directed Studies.
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB majors only; and, consent of instructor and department; and upper- division standing; and, two upper-division courses in MCDB or EEMB.
nodes.description: Hours and credit by arrangement with any faculty member.

nodes.title: Directed Readings
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB majors only; and, consent of instructor and department; and upper- division standing; and, two upper-division courses in MCDB or EEMB.
nodes.description: Individual conferences one hour every two weeks. special readings designed to broaden the outlook of students and to knit into a cohesive whole the basic principles underlying the major disciplines in the field.

nodes.title: Independent Studies

nodes.title: Medical Immunology
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 101A OR EEMB 129 with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: By focusing on recent groundbreaking advances in our understanding of the vertebrate immune system, this course explores the contrasting mechanisms of protective immunity against parasites and cancer with various immune disorders that mainly stem from immune dysregulation, such as autoimmunity, acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS), allergies, and other diseases. By engaging in interactive, case-based computer exercises, students will have an opportunity to emulate the discovery of the underlying biological defects that give rise to these and other immune-related diseases.
